title: The generic Fourier sheaf is pure of some weight
statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let $\psi$ be a
nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$
(irreducible among lisse Weil sheaves: its only lisse Weil subsheaves are
$0$ and $\mathcal M$) which is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Let $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ be a dense open immersion
into the dual line and $\mathcal M'$ a lisse Weil sheaf on $U'_0$
(such data exist by [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension]) with

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

Then $\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure, on all of $U'_0$, of some
real weight $v$ (in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights]).

proof.text:
*Step 1: the real envelope after zero extension.* Put
$b=\iota^{-1}(q^w)$, $\mathcal M^\dagger=\mathcal M^\vee\otimes\mathcal B_b$,
and let $\mathcal K$ be the realified kernel on the Fourier square formed
from $j_!\mathcal M$ and $j_!\mathcal M^\dagger$ as in
[lem-fd-realified-kernel-real]. By the general form of
[lem-fd-realified-kernel-real], which needs only the purity of
$\mathcal M$, the constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal K$ is $\iota$-real.
By [lem-fd-constituent-nonexceptional-concentration](3),
$R^\nu p_{2,!}\mathcal K=0$ for $\nu\neq1$, and the sheaf
$\mathcal G:=\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M)$ (concentrated in
degree $0$) is a direct summand of
$\mathcal H:=R^1p_{2,!}\mathcal K$. By [lem-fd-realness-pushforward],
applied to $\mathcal K$ and this vanishing, $\mathcal H$ is an
$\iota$-real constructible Weil sheaf on the dual line $A'_0$.

*Step 2: the zero-extension comparison.* By
[prop-fd-zero-extension-comparison], the hypotheses of which are exactly
those of the present statement, there is a sheaf $\mathcal G$ with
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M[1])\cong\mathcal G[1]$ and a short
exact sequence of Weil sheaves on the dual line
$$0\to\mathcal B'\to\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'\to0.$$
Here $j'_*\mathcal M'$ is the middle extension of
[def-wf-middle-extension], so the last map is an epimorphism.

*Step 3: the lisse dense open and irreducibility.* By
[prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension], applied to $\psi$, $j$ and $\mathcal M$
(nonzero, irreducible lisse Weil, constituent-nonexceptional), there are a
dense open immersion $j'':U''_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ and a nonzero
irreducible lisse Weil sheaf $\mathcal N$ on $U''_0$ with
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong(j''_*\mathcal N)[1]$.
Together with the hypothesis this gives $(j'_*\mathcal M')[1]\cong(j''_*\mathcal N)[1]$;
taking the cohomology sheaf in degree $-1$ gives an isomorphism of Weil
sheaves $j'_*\mathcal M'\cong j''_*\mathcal N$ on $A'_0$. Apply
[fin2-lem-lisse-dense-open] to $\mathcal H$ and to $\mathcal G$; on the
line $A'_0$ the complement of each lisse open is finite, so intersecting
the two opens with $U'_0\cap U''_0$ gives a dense open
$V'_0\subset U'_0\cap U''_0$ on which $\mathcal H$ and $\mathcal G$ are
lisse. For an open immersion the restriction of the direct image to the
open is the original sheaf, so restricting the isomorphism to $V'_0$ gives
$\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}\cong\mathcal N|_{V'_0}$: two lisse sheaves with
isomorphic shifted middle extensions agree on a common dense open. Since
$U''_0$ is a dense open of the affine line, it is a curve in the sense of
[lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective](4), and $V'_0$ is a nonempty open of it,
so by that clause $\mathcal N|_{V'_0}$, hence $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$, is a
nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf. Restriction of sheaves is exact, and
restricting the projection from the direct summand
$\mathcal H\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal G$ together with the epimorphism of
Step 2 (whose target restricts to $(j'_*\mathcal M')|_{V'_0}=\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$)
gives an epimorphism of lisse Weil sheaves
$$\mathcal H|_{V'_0}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}.$$

source.place: Step 3, first paragraph; and sk-p-dl-a1-some-weight.proof.md: "The transform ... is also the middle extension of an irreducible lisse sheaf, and two lisse sheaves with isomorphic shifted middle extensions agree on a common dense open"

proof.text:
*Step 4: purity on the dense open.* The sheaf $\mathcal H|_{V'_0}$ is
lisse and $\iota$-real: lissity is the choice of $V'_0$, and reality is
the pointwise condition of [def-wf-iota-real], hence survives restriction
to an open. The epimorphism of Step 3 and a finite composition series of
the finite-dimensional lisse representation show that the nonzero
irreducible sheaf $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is an irreducible constituent of
$\mathcal H|_{V'_0}$. Since $V'_0$ is a dense open of the affine line, it
is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve. Thus
[thm-rp-real-lisse-purity-affine] gives punctually $\iota$-pure weight
$v:=\dw_\iota(\mathcal M'|_{V'_0})$, with $\dw_\iota$ as in
[def-wf-determinantal-weight].

*Step 5: purity on all of $U'_0$.* The sheaf $\mathcal M'$ is lisse on
the smooth geometrically connected curve $U'_0$, and its restriction to
the dense open $V'_0$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $v$. Apply the
consequence clause of [cor-wf-unramified-boundary-purity] to the dense
open $V'_0\hookrightarrow U'_0$; it gives that $\mathcal M'$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $v$ on all of $U'_0$.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions], let $\psi$ be a
nontrivial additive character of $k_0$, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ be a dense open immersion
and let $\mathcal M$ be a nonzero irreducible lisse Weil sheaf on $U_0$
(irreducible among lisse Weil sheaves: its only lisse Weil subsheaves are
$0$ and $\mathcal M$) which is constituent-nonexceptional in the sense of
[def-a1-constituent-nonexceptional] and punctually $\iota$-pure of
weight $w$. Let $j':U'_0\hookrightarrow A'_0$ be a dense open immersion
into the dual line and $\mathcal M'$ a lisse Weil sheaf on $U'_0$
(such data exist by [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension]) with

$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi\bigl((j_*\mathcal M)[1]\bigr)\cong(j'_*\mathcal M')[1].
$$

Then $\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure, on all of $U'_0$, of some
real weight $v$ (in the sense of [def-weil-punctual-weights]).

proof.text:
*Step 1: the real envelope after zero extension.* Put
$b=\iota^{-1}(q^w)$, $\mathcal M^\dagger=\mathcal M^\vee\otimes\mathcal B_b$,
and let $\mathcal K$ be the realified kernel on the Fourier square formed
from $j_!\mathcal M$ and $j_!\mathcal M^\dagger$ as in
[lem-fd-realified-kernel-real]. By the general form of
[lem-fd-realified-kernel-real], which needs only the purity of
$\mathcal M$, the constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal K$ is $\iota$-real.
By [lem-fd-constituent-nonexceptional-concentration](3),
$R^\nu p_{2,!}\mathcal K=0$ for $\nu\neq1$, and the sheaf

$$
\mathcal G:=\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M)
$$

(concentrated in degree $0$) is a direct summand of
$\mathcal H:=R^1p_{2,!}\mathcal K$. By [lem-fd-realness-pushforward],
applied to $\mathcal K$ and this vanishing, $\mathcal H$ is an
$\iota$-real constructible Weil sheaf on the dual line $A'_0$. Working
with $j_!\mathcal M$ rather than $j_*\mathcal M$ is what makes the
reality available: at a missing point both summands of $\mathcal K$ have
zero stalk, while the boundary stalks of $j_*\mathcal M$ and
$j_*\mathcal M^\dagger$ need not have conjugate spectra.

*Step 2: $\mathcal G$ surjects onto the middle extension.* By the
zero-extension comparison [prop-fd-zero-extension-comparison], whose
hypotheses are exactly those of the present statement,
$\operatorname{FT}_\psi(j_!\mathcal M[1])\cong\mathcal G[1]$ and there is
a short exact sequence of Weil sheaves
$0\to\mathcal B'\to\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'\to0$ on the dual line,
with $j'_*\mathcal M'$ the middle extension of
[def-wf-middle-extension]. In particular
$\mathcal G\to j'_*\mathcal M'$ is an epimorphism of Weil sheaves.

*Step 3: purity on a dense open.* By [fin2-lem-lisse-dense-open],
applied to $\mathcal H$ and to $\mathcal G$ and intersected with
$U'_0$, there is a dense open $V'_0\subset U'_0$ on which $\mathcal H$
and $\mathcal G$ are lisse. Restriction to $V'_0$ is exact and additive,
and $(j'_*\mathcal M')|_{V'_0}=\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$. Composing the
projection $\mathcal H\to\mathcal G$ onto the direct summand with the
epimorphism of Step 2 gives an epimorphism of lisse Weil sheaves

$$
\mathcal H|_{V'_0}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}.
$$

The restriction $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is nonzero and irreducible: the
Weil group of the dense open $V'_0$ of the normal connected curve
$U'_0$ surjects onto that of $U'_0$ (the corresponding surjectivity of
étale fundamental groups for a dense open of a normal connected scheme,
SGA 1, Exp. V, 8.2), so the invariant subspaces are the same. Refining
the kernel of this epimorphism to a composition series of
$\mathcal H|_{V'_0}$ shows that $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is an irreducible
constituent of $\mathcal H|_{V'_0}$, which is lisse and $\iota$-real
([def-wf-iota-real]; reality is a pointwise condition and passes to
the open). As $V'_0$ is a dense open of the affine line, it is a smooth
geometrically connected affine curve, and
[thm-rp-real-lisse-purity-affine] shows that $\mathcal M'|_{V'_0}$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of the real weight
$v:=\dw_\iota(\mathcal M'|_{V'_0})$, its determinantal weight of
[def-wf-determinantal-weight].

*Step 4: purity on all of $U'_0$.* The sheaf $\mathcal M'$ is lisse on
the smooth geometrically connected curve $U'_0$ and its restriction to
the dense open $V'_0$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $v$. At a
point $x\in U'_0\setminus V'_0$ the inertia acts trivially, $\mathcal M'$
being lisse there, and the ordinary direct image from $V'_0$ recovers the
stalk of $\mathcal M'$ (the translation step of
[lem-a1-constituent-nonexceptional-comparison]). The consequence
clause of [cor-wf-unramified-boundary-purity] therefore gives that
$\mathcal M'$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $v$ on all of
$U'_0$.

split_report.summary: Aligned the item with the main-20261015 blueprint by adding the explicit nontrivial additive character and lisse-partner wording. Reworked the proof into five steps: the realified kernel, zero-extension comparison, derivation of the partner's irreducibility from Fourier t-exactness and the simple-object classification, dense-open real purity, and extension across the lisse boundary. Reused the existing dense-open fundamental-group/Weil-group surjectivity node; no new nodes were needed. Maintainer reader (2026-10-18): Step 3 now derives the irreducibility of the given partner on the dense open by comparing it with the irreducible partner of [prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension], as the main-20261015 unit proof does, instead of through the perverse simple-object classification and t-exact equivalence; the explanatory citation of the Fourier trace formula in Step 1 was removed (the realified-kernel lemma states the reality used); the source metadata now names the main-20261015 files and no SGA document.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1, 2, 3 first paragraph, 3 second paragraph, and 4 of the blueprint proof are realized respectively by item steps 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.

tool_uses.why: The generic dense-open fundamental-group/Weil-group surjectivity and preservation of irreducibility are supplied by the existing purity-real-sheaves lemma; the Fourier-weight unit has no replacement for this generic tool.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-a74e7b377 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the main-20261015 source, the unit proof and every cited statement in full; there are no new nodes. The statement is the main-20261015 text verbatim: ψ is nontrivial and the partner M′ is any lisse sheaf. I tested it on the Kummer case U=G_m, M=L_χ, where M′ is pure of weight 1. Steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 are correct: the general clause of the realified-kernel lemma applies, as do concentration (3), the realness pushforward, the zero-extension comparison (a dense open of A¹ has finite complement), real-lisse purity on the dense open V′, and the consequence clause of cor-wf-unramified-boundary-purity. I repaired three faults in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/thm-fd-generic-fourier-sheaf-pure.json. (1) C4/batch-5: Step 1 cited sk-thm-fourier-trace-formula, whose proof is the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula, only as decoration, since the kernel lemma itself states the reality. I removed the citation and its tool_use. (2) E5/C3: in Step 3, the perverse simple-object classification only gives that the transform is a middle extension of some irreducible N; the comparison of M′ with N was missing, and the step tacitly used the t-exact equivalence on Weil objects. I rewrote the step along the main-20261015 unit route. prop-a1-fourier-middle-extension gives an irreducible N; taking H^{-1} gives j′_*M′≅j″_*N; restricting to a dense V′⊂U′∩U″ gives M′|V′≅N|V′, which is irreducible by clause (4) of lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective. This drops the citations of thm-a1-fourier-t-exact and prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples. (3) The source metadata named the old master snapshot and an imported SGA 1 external entry (route lock); I updated source and proof_origin to the main-20261015 files. Batch-5 check, citation by citation: rem-dl-a1-conventions is a conventions definition and is accepted. lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective reaches only the general lisse-to-representation dictionary, is on the transitive route, and its tool_use is accepted. sk-thm-fourier-trace-formula is removed. thm-a1-fourier-t-exact and prop-a1-curve-perverse-simples are removed, and they would have been acceptable since they reach only definitions. Every remaining citation is on the unit's transitive route.
